newsitem.title: INDIA: India court extends deadline for "Bandit Queen".
newsitem.headline: India court extends deadline for "Bandit Queen".

text.p: An Indian court on Monday gave former "Bandit Queen" Phoolan Devi two more weeks to appear in response to a summons, which she has ignored so far, after a deadline passed with no news of her whereabouts.
Devi, a member of parliament, is wanted in 57 cases, including murder. On February 4 Devi ignored a summons to appear in court, where she faced arrest warrants in the pending cases.
"The validity of the warrant will remain extended until March 3," Judge S.K. Srivastava said in Kanpur, about 100 km (62 miles) from Lucknow, capital of the state of Uttar Pradesh.
Police have not arrested Devi despite a nationwide alert and have been unable to find her despite raids on two of her homes.
The government of Uttar Pradesh appealed 10 days ago to India's Supreme Court to overturn the lower court's summons. The nation's highest court is yet to give a ruling on the appeal.
Devi's lawyer Nand Lal Jaiswal has said Devi has no plans to surrender to police.

Movie maker Sekhar Kapoor portrayed Devi, who belongs to the low-caste Mallah community of boatmen, as a heroine who seeks revenge on her rapists in the film "Bandit Queen," which won acclaim at several international film festivals.
Devi shot to notoriety after 22 upper-caste men were killed in a massacre at the northern Indian village of Behmai in 1981.
She was accused of leading a gang in the massacre but denied the charges.
Devi surrendered to police in 1983 under an amnesty offered by the central state of Madhya Pradesh. She spent more than 10 years in prison before being released on parole in 1994.

The chief minister of Uttar Pradesh then withdrew all cases against her and inducted her into his Samajwadi Party, a regional socialist party which represents low castes. She won a seat in parliamentary elections last May.
Devi faced fresh police action when the state's high court revived the cases against her after a man who claimed to be one of her intended victims asked that they be reinstated.
On February 4, the court rejected a demand by Devi's lawyer to withdraw the arrest warrants, and ordered police to produce her in court on February 17.
